title: Unified Inference: Product Overview, PRD, Design Specs, Roadmap & Pricing (Comprehensive)
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview:

This comprehensive Confluence document consolidates the product overview, product requirements (PRD), core design specifications, roadmap & themes, pricing and packaging notes, and release notes for the Unified Inference product family. Intended audience: product managers, engineering, solutions/SE, sales, and customer success.

Executive summary:
- Goal: Provide a single canonical reference describing what Unified Inference delivers, why customers choose it, the implementation approach, milestone plan for the next 4 quarters, pricing/packaging strategy, and the operational playbook for releases.
- Target customers: mid-market and enterprise product teams, AI-native startups, and platform teams who need predictable latency, cost controls, and deployment flexibility.

Business objectives and success metrics:
1) Reduce median 99th-percentile latency for typical chat workloads by 20% for hosted API customers by end of Q4 2027.
2) Achieve 30% adoption of Redwood Optimize suggestions among existing dedicated customers within 6 months of release.
3) Hit $X M ARR from Dedicated contracts within 12 months following pricing refresh.
4) Maintain platform availability SLA of 99.95% (monthly) for Dedicated customers.

Product overview (high-level):
- Core product family: Redwood API (hosted), Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity), Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem), Redwood Console (observability & ops), Redwood Optimize (cost/performance toolkit).
- Primary capabilities: text generation (sync+streaming), chat, embeddings, reranking, function/tool calling, model catalog and versioning, automated batching/caching, and smart routing/fallbacks.

Problem statements (why this matters):
- Customers face unpredictable inference economics as workloads scale: variable per-token latency and cost across models and hardware.
- Operational complexity: teams must stitch tooling for rollouts, tracing, and regression detection across deployments.
- Compliance and data residency requirements push customers to hybrid/private deployments while retaining unified observability.

Key user personas and primary user stories:
- ML Engineer (platform): "As an ML engineer I want deterministic latency and cost estimates so I can capacity plan and meet SLA commitments."
- Product Engineer: "As a product engineer I want simple SDKs and route-level feature flags (canary/A-B) so I can safely ship updates."
- Platform Lead: "As a platform lead I want a single pane of glass for tracing and cost allocation across teams and models."

Product requirements (PRD summary):
- RQ-001: Unified API parity across Hosted/Dedicated/Private for text-generation, embeddings, and function calling. (Must support identical request/response shapes and identical SDK methods.)
- RQ-002: Streaming response support with backpressure handling and stable connection behavior for >10k concurrent streams per region.
- RQ-003: Model catalog with verified performance profiles: provide latency/cost-per-token baseline for each model variant and quantization profile.
- RQ-004: Smart routing policies: latency-first, cost-first, and region affinity. Policies configurable per-customer and per-route.
- RQ-005: Redwood Optimize recommendations engine capable of suggesting batching, cache TTLs, and quantization profiles - target 10% cost reduction for text generation workloads.
- RQ-006: Rollout primitives: canary (10% traffic), A/B (split), automatic fallback to compatible variant when error rate or latency breach detected.
- RQ-007: Observability: token-level cost breakdown, per-route P50/P95/P99 latency, and user-visible trace IDs preserved end-to-end.
- RQ-008: Security/compliance: KMS integration for Private deployments and audit logs with immutable storage for 365 days (configurable).

Non-functional requirements:
- Perf NFR-001: 99th-percentile token latency for short-chat (<=256 tokens) under typical load: <120ms for hosted P2 instances equivalent.
- Scalability NFR-002: Support autoscaling from 0.1x to 10x baseline traffic with sub-2-minute scale-up time for Dedicated pools.
- Reliability NFR-003: Degrade gracefully: service must provide model-variant fallback and regional failover with <2% request loss during capacity incidents.

Design specifications (summary):
Architecture overview:
- High-level components: API gateway, routing/orchestration layer, serving runtime (GPU-optimized inference engine), compilation/kernel selector, cache layer (prefix + KV cache), metrics & tracing pipeline, control plane for catalog and rollout configs.
- Dataflow: requests arrive at API gateway -> authentication + quota -> routing policy evaluation -> serve on runtime instance (with KV cache consult) -> streaming return via gateway.

API contract (example):
- POST /v1/generate
  Request fields: model (string), input (string|array), max_tokens (int), temperature (float), stream (bool), route (optional string)
  Response: streaming token envelopes (when stream=true) with fields: token, token_index, partial_text, trace_id, model_version

Example request JSON snippet:
{
  "model": "redwood-2.8b-q4",
  "input": "Summarize the customer feedback below.",
  "max_tokens": 150,
  "temperature": 0.0,
  "stream": true
}

Routing & fallback behavior:
- Each request evaluates policy in this order: route override -> customer policy -> global default.
- If chosen model experiences resource constraints, runtime will automatically select the nearest-compatible variant that satisfies constraints (quantized variant or larger-latency variant depending on policy).

Configuration table (sample):
- Route config fields: name, default_model, policy (latency/cost/region), canary_percent, cache_enabled, max_concurrency, owner
- Example row: name=chat-prod, default_model=redwood-2.8b-q4, policy=latency-first, canary_percent=10, cache_enabled=true, max_concurrency=1000, owner=team-chat

Design trade-offs and notes:
- We prioritize parity of API across deployment modes at the cost of additional control-plane complexity.
- Aggressive caching improves cost but requires conservative TTL defaults to avoid stale context in multi-turn chat.

Roadmap & themes (next 4 quarters):
- Themes: Performance & Predictability, Cost Optimization, Enterprise Trusted Deployments, Developer Experience.
- Q3 2027 (now): finish Redwood Optimize v3 rollout, finalize model catalog performance profiles, launch initial canary for unified streaming contract.
- Q4 2027: Dedicated autoscaling improvements, new quantization profiles for 8-bit and 4-bit variants, pricing refresh for Dedicated commitments.
- Q1 2028: Private on-prem packaged installer (air-gapped), advanced RBAC for Console, and long-term retention for audit logs (customer-configurable).
- Q2 2028: Cross-region active-active failover, improved batching heuristics integrated into runtime, expanded billing attribution per-tenant & per-route.

Milestones and success criteria:
- Milestone M-2027-09-30: Redwood Optimize v3 GA adoption metric >= 15% of eligible customers.
- Milestone M-2027-12-15: Pricing refresh for Dedicated published and communicated to sales; pilot customers onboarded.

Pricing & packaging notes (strategy):
- Principles: predictable committed pricing for Dedicated; usage-based for Hosted; modular add-ons (observability retention, compliance packages).
- Packaging tiers (simplified):
  * Hosted - Pay-as-you-go: per-token generation + per-embedding unit. No committed SLA. Includes basic Console features.
  * Dedicated - Reserved capacity: monthly commit (vCPU/GPU equivalent units), discounted unit price, 99.95% SLA, premium support add-on.
  * Private - Enterprise license: platform fee + deployment support + optional on-prem bundle.

Pricing table (example):
- Hosted:
  * Generation: $0.0009 / token (base model), $0.0018 / token (large model)
  * Embeddings: $0.003 / 1k vectors
- Dedicated (example committed rates):
  * Small pool (4x A100 equiv): $12,000 / month (commit) - effective token cost ~ $0.0005
  * Medium pool (16x A100 equiv): $42,000 / month - effective token cost ~ $0.00035
- Add-ons:
  * Extended observability (13 months retention): +$2,500 / month
  * Compliance package (SOC2+ISO): one-time setup $15,000 + $1,000 / month

Notes on packaging and sales motion:
- Self-serve for Hosted; sales-assisted Dedicated with usage thresholds (e.g., usage > $25k/month triggers commercial outreach).
- Migration credits for pilot Dedicated customers to offset migration costs.

Release notes and rollout plan (current release: unified-inference v2.4 - release date 2027-08-15):
- Highlights:
  * GA: Unified streaming API across Hosted and Dedicated.
  * Feature: Redwood Optimize v3 recommendations integrated into Console with per-route suggestions.
  * Perf: Kernel selector improvements that reduce P99 token latency by 12% on average for 2.8B models.
- Migration notes for customers:
  * Clients using legacy streaming endpoints should switch to /v1/generate with stream=true. SDK updates available v4.2.
  * If customers rely on custom rollout logic, map previous rollout flags to new 'route' config with minimal changes.
- Rollout plan:
  1) Stage: internal canary (engineering + solutions) for 72 hours.
  2) Stage: 5% external canary for low-risk customers (24 hours monitoring).
  3) Stage: 25% rollout with automated rollback criteria.
  4) Stage: 100% global rollout with post-release monitoring.
- Canary/rollback criteria:
  * Error rate > 2x baseline for 10 minutes -> rollback.
  * P99 latency increase > 40% for 15 minutes -> rollback.
  * Token-level cost increase > 20% for 30 minutes -> investigate and hold rollout.

Telemetry & monitoring plan:
- Dashboards: per-route latency (P50/P95/P99), error rates, cost per 1M tokens, streaming connection health.
- Alerts: sustained error rate spike (>1.5x baseline for 5 minutes), streaming disconnect rate > 1% of active sessions, autoscaler failure.

Operational runbook (high-level):
1) Detection: alert triggers on Console -> oncall SRE notified.
2) Triage: owner inspects trace IDs, recent deploys, and routing decisions.
3) Mitigation: implement rollback via release manager OR apply routing override to route traffic to fallback model variant.
4) Postmortem: create postmortem within 72 hours and schedule follow-up action items.

Open risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Quantization regressions may introduce quality regressions for hallucination-sensitive flows.
  Mitigation: require evaluation harness (prompt + ground truth) and automatic regression alerting before recommending quantized variant.
- Risk: Pricing confusion across committed Dedicated tiers.
  Mitigation: provide clear migration worksheets and TCO calculators in sales toolkit.

Appendix: detailed requirement IDs and acceptance criteria:
- RQ-001 acceptance: SDK parity tests pass (100% of canonical API tests), integration tests for Hosted, Dedicated, Private.
- RQ-002 acceptance: streaming load test with 10k concurrent producers results below 2% dropped frames and P99 latency <250ms.

If there are questions about any section, please reach out to the product owner or the listed engineering leads. This page will be updated after each major milestone and as pricing / legal guidance is finalized.
